questions.question: A trailer brake hand valve on a truck can be used to:

options.text: Add fuel to the vehicle.
Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
Check the oil level.
Load cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling backward when you start from a stop.

questions.question: When turning, when should you cancel the turn signal?

options.text: Before entering the turn
During the turn
After the turn is completed

questions.correctAnswerText: After the turn is completed
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on the whole time you are turning. Turn it off only after you finish the turn.

questions.question: You should stop and take a break ____ to avoid getting too tired while driving.

options.text: Every half hour
Every hour
Every two hours
Every six hours

questions.correctAnswerText: Every two hours
questions.explanation: Take a break at least once every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: After an accident, flares should be used with caution because:

options.text: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares in sunny weather.
Flares are expensive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fuel may be spilled on the ground and could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Flares near spilled fuel can cause vehicle fires. Use flares carefully after an accident.

questions.question: When using your mirrors, you should look at your tires frequently to:

options.text: Watch for tire fires.
See if the tires are rolling properly.
Check if the tread is good enough.
Compare tire size to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for tire fires.
questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to notice a tire fire early. Tire fires happen when tires are under-inflated, dual tires touch, or tires overheat.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a way to prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Getting enough sleep before driving
Traveling with a passenger
Driving during hours when you would normally be asleep
Avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving during hours when you would normally be asleep
questions.explanation: To stay alert, get a full night's sleep before driving, travel with someone to share driving duties, drive during times you are normally awake, and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Can replace flat mirrors.
Help you see a wider area.
Are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Curved convex mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only comes from physical distraction, not mental distraction.
Is made worse when you pre-program radio stations.
Can be avoided by eating while driving.
Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be avoided by not having complex conversations while driving.
questions.explanation: Avoid complex or emotionally charged conversations while driving. Pre-program radio stations before your trip and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving. Mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical ones.

questions.question: Rules about passenger comfort, like smoking, should:

options.text: Only be mentioned if someone breaks a rule.
Only be mentioned if a passenger asks.
Be announced at the start of the trip.
Be discussed one-on-one with each passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be announced at the start of the trip.
questions.explanation: Many bus services have rules about smoking, drinking, and music devices. Explaining these rules at the beginning of a trip helps prevent problems later.

questions.question: Which of the following surfaces is the most slippery?

options.text: Dry ice
Wet ice
Wet pavement

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet ice
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when the weather warms just enough to slightly melt the ice. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: How long does it take an average driver to react?

options.text: One-sixteenth of a second
One-eighth of a second
Between three-quarters and one full second
Two seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters and one full second
questions.explanation: Most drivers take between three-quarters and one full second to react.

questions.question: Why should you open the front door when stopping at a railroad crossing?

options.text: It helps you hear an approaching train better.
You should never do this.
Other noises entering the bus make it harder to hear trains.
It takes too long and is not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you hear an approaching train better.
questions.explanation: Open the front door at a railroad crossing only if it helps you see or hear an approaching train.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look while driving?

options.text: Two to three seconds ahead
Five to six seconds ahead
12 to 15 seconds ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds ahead
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of their vehicle. This gives you time to spot and respond to dangers before you reach them. Watch for vehicles entering the highway, changing into your lane, or turning.

questions.question: Why should you back a trailer toward the driver's side?

options.text: You will have the best view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can help on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have the best view.
questions.explanation: When backing up, always back toward the driver's left side. This gives you the best view of the back of your vehicle.

questions.question: What must buses never carry?

options.text: Small arms ammunition
Soft drinks
Open food
Tear gas

questions.correctAnswerText: Tear gas
questions.explanation: Buses must never carry tear gas or other irritating materials, even though they can carry some hazardous materials under certain conditions.

questions.question: What should a driver do before driving a bus that has been parked for several days?

options.text: Assume the inside is in good condition.
Call the local police to inspect the bus.
Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
questions.explanation: Parked buses can get damaged. Before driving, check the inside of the bus to make sure all important systems work and passengers are safe.

questions.question: What is the standee line?

options.text: A line on the bus floor that passengers cannot cross.
A single line of standing passengers.
A mark showing the maximum number of people allowed on the bus.
A mark showing how tall passengers can be.

questions.correctAnswerText: A line on the bus floor that passengers cannot cross.
questions.explanation: While a bus is moving, passengers cannot stand in front of the driver's seat. A two-inch line on the floor (or another clear marker) shows where passengers must not go. This is called the standee line.

questions.question: When should you sign a previous driver's inspection report?

options.text: When the previous driver dated their entry.
When reported defects have been fixed.
When you will drive longer than one hour or more than 50 miles.
When the report is on the dashboard.

questions.correctAnswerText: When reported defects have been fixed.
questions.explanation: Only sign a previous inspection report if any noted defects have been fixed or if no repairs were needed.

questions.question: What should the coolant temperature gauge do when you start a vehicle?

options.text: Stay in the same position
Slowly rise to normal operating temperature
Jump quickly to normal operating temperature
Flash until it reaches normal operating temperature

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly rise to normal operating temperature
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after starting the engine. The coolant temperature gauge should slowly rise to the normal operating range.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report informs the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.
